title: Molecular Binding Energy Calorimeter
description: A virtual calorimetry lab where the coffee mat serves as a heated reaction platform, the corset model represents a flexible molecular cage catalyst, and the shoe model represents a ligand donor molecule. Users drag reagent spheres onto the platform, adjust catalyst compression and ligand orientation, then measure exothermic/endothermic energy changes while obeying conservation of energy across all coupled subsystems.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a molecular calorimetry simulation. Load three GLB assets using GLTFLoader: coffeemat.glb placed flat at y=0 as the heated reaction platform with a glowing emissive material whose color shifts from blue (cold) to red (hot) based on current energy; Corset.glb scaled to 0.3 and floating above the platform at y=1.5 representing a compressible molecular cage catalyst; MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb placed to the right at x=2 representing a ligand donor molecule that can be rotated to expose different binding sites. Use OrbitControls for camera at position (0,3,6) looking at origin. Add ambient light intensity 0.4 and two directional lights. Create a UI panel (HTML overlay) showing: total system energy (starts at 500 kJ, conserved), platform temperature, catalyst compression percentage, ligand orientation angle, and reaction log. Implement these interactions: (1) Click platform to add reagent spheres (small colored spheres, max 4 types: H2, O2, N2, CO2) that snap to grid positions on the mat. (2) Drag vertically on the corset to compress/expand it (scale y from 0.2 to 1.0), which changes catalyst activation energy threshold. (3) Click the shoe to cycle through material variants representing different ligand binding configurations. (4) Rotate the shoe around y-axis by dragging horizontally to set binding angle (0-360). (5) A React button triggers the reaction: energy transfers between reagents based on catalyst compression and ligand angle, obeying conservation of total energy. Platform temperature updates and emissive color changes. (6) Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y that reverts any of the above steps using a state history stack storing snapshots of all reagent positions, compression, angle, energy distribution, and temperature. (7) Display floating 3D text labels above each reagent showing its current energy. (8) Add particle effects on the platform during reactions. Ensure total energy is always conserved across platform heat, reagent energies, and catalyst potential energy. Minimum 10 distinct interaction steps to complete a full reaction cycle.
